subject: general
question: The second five-year plan was primarily based on which economic model?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahalanobis model**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The second five-year plan (1956-1961) of India was primarily based on the **Mahalanobis model**, formulated by the Indian statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis.
 
• This model focused on the rapid industrialization of India, with special emphasis on the development of heavy industries and the production of capital goods.
 
• The Mahalanobis model was designed to strengthen India’s industrial base and reduce dependence on foreign imports, thus promoting self-reliance.
 
• The plan aimed at allocating a larger share of resources to the industrial sector compared to agriculture, under the assumption that industrial growth would eventually stimulate agricultural and overall economic development.
 
• It introduced the idea of a planned economy and was influenced by socialist principles, emphasizing the need for state intervention in economic activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harrod-Domar Model**
 
 
• This model, proposed by economists Roy Harrod and Evsey Domar, is primarily concerned with economic growth and savings.
 
• It emphasizes the importance of investment and capital accumulation in driving economic growth.
 
• The Harrod-Domar model laid the foundation for many development theories but was not directly implemented in India’s second five-year plan.
 
• It assumes that economic growth is determined by the savings rate and the productivity of capital, represented by the capital-output ratio.
 
 
 
• **Feldman Model**
 
 
• This model was developed by Soviet economist Grigory Feldman and focused on the allocation of resources between the production of consumer goods and capital goods.
 
• It was aimed at achieving long-term economic growth by prioritizing the production of capital goods.
 
• While the Feldman model influenced the Mahalanobis model, it was not directly implemented in India.
 
• The emphasis on heavy industries in the Mahalanobis model drew inspiration from Feldman’s ideas.
 
 
 
• **Keynesian Model**
 
 
• Proposed by economist John Maynard Keynes, this model is centered around government intervention to manage demand in the economy.
 
• It is primarily concerned with short-term economic fluctuations, emphasizing fiscal policies and public spending to stimulate economic growth.
 
• The Keynesian model was not the basis for India’s second five-year plan, as it focused on industrial development and long-term growth rather than short-term demand management.
 
 
 
• **Second Five-Year Plan**
 
 
• The second five-year plan was pivotal in shaping India’s industrial policy and aimed at transforming the country into a self-reliant economy.
 
• It was heavily influenced by socialist principles and sought to reduce income inequality through state-led initiatives.
 
• The plan also marked a shift from agricultural development to industrialization as the primary driver of economic growth.
